item_verdicts.write_paths: all 5 changed paths are inside the 6 declared write paths - scan_local_lane_deaths.py, local-lane-deaths.json, local-lane-death-rate.html, test_the_local_lane_death_rate_is_stated.py and the evidence fragment - and the 6th, docs/figures/a-review-dies-where-nobody-is-looking/death-shape-correlation, is granted but unused, which the brief requires rather than merely permits: it states the done-when names an artifact so the node may write that artifact and 'permits no other figure and no evidence prose'; the worktree is clean at e706dcae2 and no peer node's path was touched.

justifications.durability: the new assertion is a real guard, not a green line: I reinstated the declared regression in my reading of the code - the scanner reads exit_signals(entry) at scan_local_lane_deaths.py:478 and folding {} there empties every block - and the run's own negative control shows that exactly that mutation reddens this test at the headline-cell guard (1 failed, 6 passed, EXIT=1, first line matching the declared string verbatim), which is the failure the assertion's own message predicts; the residual is that the sums compare one part of the file against another part the same fold produced, so a systematically wrong but internally consistent reader would satisfy them, and the test's own answer to that - with_exit_record > 0 and the tie to the positive control's SIGTERM, whose run is a review at xhigh and so sits inside the headline cell - is what keeps the block from being verified only by itself; the page's headline split (91 SIGTERM / 39 SIGKILL among the 130) is stated in prose and pinned by no assertion, since the test checks only that deaths_signalled equals the sum of deaths_signals_by_name.
justifications.evidence: the done_when's measure is recorded rather than claimed, and I checked the receipts rather than their absence: the file names the scan's own revision by content digest and tree revision (method.scan_revision) and sha256sum of the committed scanner reproduces 03d7f845..., so the datum is tied to the bytes that read the corpus; I derived the added-failure count from the reviewed manifest's own baseline_suite and after_suite logs through reckon.crew.review.annotate_review_of_run - 0 added, ids [] - and, because a zero is a claim about the instrument, showed the same derivation returns 1 with the id it names when a single FAILED line is appended to the after arm's text; I re-ran the named gate at head myself (7 passed, EXIT=0, logs/review-head-gate.log) rather than resting on the worker's summary; and the negative control's first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim while its last line is a bare EXIT=1. The cost is the fragment's stale head-arm revision, reported as a finding.
justifications.fit: the change matches the module it lands in - the new helpers sit beside exit_signals and stream_facts in the same shape, names state the mechanism (recorded_signal, fold_exit_record, render_exit_records, signal_exit_record) with no plan, sprint or ticket identifier and no attribution anywhere in source, commits or the fragment; subjects are conventional with substantive bodies (feat/data/docs/docs); the page's section numbering was carried through honestly when a new §3 was inserted (old §3 to §4, §4 to §5, §5 to §6); and the block states its own coverage denominator rather than letting a share read as a population, which is the idiom this page already holds.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the landed change does exactly what the goal states and stops there, adding no deliverable the goal does not imply: the scanner emits the exit-record count and signal breakdown per cell, for the review role at every effort and corpus-wide (render_exit_records called for exactly those three populations), and the page states the signalled share of review deaths from that file - 130 of 392, 33.2%, 91 SIGTERM and 39 SIGKILL - which I reproduced from the committed JSON (deaths_signals_by_name {SIGTERM: 91, SIGKILL: 39}, deaths_with_exit_record 130 of 392).
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff is five paths, all inside the declared write paths, and it carries nothing the goal does not imply; the 6th granted path, the figures directory, is correctly left empty because the brief forbids a figure the done-when does not name, and the manifest's follow_ons name the stale chart and the plot script rather than reaching for them - both outside the fence, and both named as such after checking the grant list.
